final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the argument around the same record. That reframing is useful, but it does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate. A caveated certification position would only support compliant_with_caveats if admissible evidence showed the caveat had been operationalized through an actual reviewed disclosure artifact, exclusion of the affected use case, or approved risk acceptance. None of those conditions is evidenced here. The current record still shows an exposed below-target aviation maintenance triage segment, no approved segment-specific risk acceptance, and no proof that the required disclosure package is in place before launch. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and staged rollout with rollback support operational risk management, but under the stated policy they do not cure the disclosure and approval gap.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure artifact was finalized, reviewed, or attached to the launch decision.
The aviation maintenance triage segment remains below target on deferred-defect routing and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no approved risk-acceptance record addressing the exposed aviation maintenance triage segment; the available record is only an incomplete draft.
Policy states rollout controls, rollback, dashboards, or a small initial percentage do not substitute for exclusion or approved risk acceptance when the affected segment remains exposed.
